text:
Sanjay: Heads-up — customer X hit a 6s tail latency spike yesterday and our rate limiter dropped a bunch of keys. digging in now.
Eva: saw the alert. was that the short 10s surge or sustained? logs looked like a microburst pattern to me.
Sanjay: short spike (~12s) followed by steady lower throughput. token bucket drained and keys hit hard throttles. we didn't apply any short-window grace.
Marie: are we using token-bucket or leaky-bucket semantics for per-key enforcement right now? last I checked we had token-bucket for burst, leaky for overall shaping.
Alex: enforcement flow: per-key token-bucket for instant burst, org-level leaky-bucket style smoothing in front for steady-state. but mixing semantics is confusing in code.
Jen: suggestion: add a tiny ephemeral grace pool for 200ms-2s to avoid killing short UI-driven spikes. customers expect small spikes to pass.
Sanjay: agree. but concern: grace pools can be abused to extend burst lifespan if not decayed quickly.
Eva: what if we use EWMA refill adaptation + a penalty-decay that halves grace tokens every 30s after use? that limits sustained exploitation.
Marie: prototype config idea (TL;DR):

```
rate_limit:
  per_key:
    refill_rate: 50/s
    burst_capacity: 300
    ephemeral_grace: 150  # short window tokens
    grace_window_ms: 1500
    grace_penalty_half_life_s: 30
  org_shaper:
    leak_rate: 1000/s
    bucket_capacity: 5000
```

Alex: looks reasonable. if ephemeral_grace is only usable once per grace_window and decays fast we should be safe.
Jen: need telemetry to validate. propose adding metrics: short_burst_count (<=2s), short_burst_accepted, short_burst_rejected, grace_usage_by_key, grace_decay_actions, sustained_throttle_count.
Sanjay: + trace context: when grace is applied annotate traces so we can follow downstream latency impact. add a tag like rate_limiter.grace=true
ops-bot: automated note: created alert rule ephemeral_grace_abuse if grace_usage_by_key > 5/min for >1m.
Eva: dashboard UX: add a small sparkline for each org with two series: short_burst_accept_rate and sustained_accept_rate. allow toggling to see per-key hotspots.
Marie: rollout plan: canary to internal orgs -> 5 customers with different traffic shapes -> broader opt-in -> auto-enable after 2w if no abuse signals.
Alex: API debate: should grace be opt-in at API key level (customer toggle) or opt-out? opt-in safe but friction for new users.
Jen: default off for low-trust tier, on for trusted keys. Console should show a toggle and estimated cost/latency impact.
Sanjay: implementation notes: keep enforcement central in quota-service not at edge to avoid inconsistent behavior across regions. but we need a tiny fast path at edge to reject clearly over-limit requests.
Eva: also sample 1/100 requests for full telemetry payloads to avoid huge egress cost. aggregated counters still required at 1s resolution for burst detection.
Marie: can we add a canary flag in the client SDK to simulate grace without charging tokens? helpful for testing without cost impact.
Alex: yes — server will honor a debug header x-rw-simulate-grace for internal tests only.
Jen: follow-up: I'll make a dashboard mock and prod config change PR. target: canary next Tue. anyone want to pair on the alert thresholds?
Sanjay: I can pair Mon afternoon. also please add a smoke test for burst_handling in the integration suite.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rate-limiter/ephemeral-grace-proto -> staging (build #4821)
ops-bot: reminder: add runbook entry for grace-related incidents (how to revert grace, how to identify abuse).
Marie: cool. meeting after lunch tomorrow to finalize numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
